exam.title: 2011年全国硕士研究生入学统一考试英语（二）真题

passages.title: Section I: Use of English
passages.content:
The Internet affords anonymity to its users, a blessing to privacy and freedom of speech. But that very anonymity is also behind the explosion of cyber-crime that has [1] across the Web.

Can privacy be preserved [2] bringing safety and security to a world that seems increasingly [3]?

Last month, Howard Schmidt, the nation's cyber-czar, offered the federal government a [4] to make the Web a safer place — a "voluntary trusted identity" system that would be the high-tech [5] of a physical key, a fingerprint and a photo ID card, all rolled [6] one. The system might use a smart identity card, or a digital credential [7] to a specific computer, and would authenticate users at a range of online services.

The idea is to [8] a federation of private online identity systems. Users could [9] which system to join, and only registered users whose identities have been authenticated could navigate those systems. The approach contrasts with one that would require an Internet driver's license [10] by the government.

Google and Microsoft are among companies that already have these "single sign-on" systems that make it possible for users to [11] just once but use many different services.

[12], the approach would create a "walled garden" in cyberspace, with safe "neighborhoods" and bright "streetlights" to establish a sense of a [13] community.

Mr. Schmidt described it as a "voluntary ecosystem" in which "individuals and organizations can complete online transactions with [14], trusting the identities of each other and the identities of the infrastructure [15] which the transaction runs."

Still, the administration's plan has [16] privacy rights activists. Some applaud the approach; others are concerned. It seems clear that such a scheme is an initiative push toward what would [17] be a compulsory Internet "driver's license" mentality.

The plan has also been greeted with [18] by some computer security experts, who worry that the "voluntary ecosystem" envisioned by Mr. Schmidt would still leave much of the Internet [19]. They argue that all Internet users should be [20] to register and identify themselves, in the same way that drivers must be licensed to drive on public roads.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs's board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University. For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism. But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked? By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board. The position was just taking up too much time, she said.

Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board. Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive's proposals. If the sky, and the share price, is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.

The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004. Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next. The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those "surprise" disappearances by directors under the age of 70. They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%. The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse. The effect tended to be larger for larger firms. Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship. Often they "trade up," leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.

But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred. Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives. Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
Whatever happened to the death of newspapers? A year ago the end seemed near. The recession threatened to remove the advertising and readers that had not already fled to the internet. Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom. America's Federal Trade Commission launched a round of talks about how to save newspapers. Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them? It will hold another meeting soon. But the discussions now seem out of date.

In much of the world there is little sign of crisis. German and Brazilian papers have shrugged off the recession. Even American newspapers, which inhabit the most troubled corner of the global industry, have not only survived but often returned to profit. Not the 20% profit margins that were routine a few years ago, but profit all the same.

It has not been much fun. Many papers stayed afloat by pushing journalists overboard. The American Society of News Editors reckons that 13,500 newsroom jobs have gone since 2007. Readers are paying more for slimmer products. Some papers even had the nerve to refuse delivery to distant suburbs. Yet these desperate measures have proved the right ones and, sadly for many journalists, they can be pushed further.

Newspapers are becoming more balanced businesses, with a healthier mix of revenues from readers and advertisers. American papers have long been highly unusual in their reliance on ads. Fully 87% of their revenues came from advertising in 2008, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation & Development (OECD). In Japan the proportion is 35%. Not surprisingly, Japanese newspapers are much more stable.

The whirlwind that swept through newsrooms harmed everybody, but much of the damage has been concentrated in areas where newspapers are least distinctive. Car and film reviewers have gone. So have science and general business reporters. Foreign bureaus have been savagely cut off. Newspapers are less complete as a result. But completeness is no longer a virtue in the newspaper business.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
We tend to think of the decades immediately following World War II as a time of prosperity and growth, with soldiers returning home by the millions, going off to college on the G. I. Bill and lining up at the marriage bureaus.

But when it came to their houses, it was a time of common sense and a belief that less could truly be more. During the Depression and the war, Americans had learned to live with less, and that restraint, in combination with the postwar confidence in the future, made small, efficient housing positively stylish.

Economic condition was only a stimulus for the trend toward efficient living. The phrase "less is more" was actually first popularized by a German, the architect Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who like other people associated with the Bauhaus, a school of design, emigrated to the United States before World War II and took up posts at American architecture schools. These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture, but none more so than Mies.

Mies's signature phrase means that less decoration, properly organized, has more impact than a lot. Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance. Like other modern architects, he employed metal, glass and laminated wood — materials that we take for granted today but that in the 1940s symbolized the future. Mies's sophisticated presentation masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty.

The apartments in the elegant towers Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive, for example, were smaller — two-bedroom units under 1,000 square feet — than those in their older neighbors along the city's Gold Coast. But they were popular because of their airy glass walls, the views they afforded and the elegance of the buildings' details and proportions, the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time.

The trend toward "less" was not entirely foreign. In the 1930s Frank Lloyd Wright started building more modest and efficient houses — usually around 1,200 square feet — than the spreading two-story ones he had designed in the 1890s and the early 20th century.

The "Case Study Houses" commissioned from talented modern architects by California Arts & Architecture magazine between 1945 and 1962 were yet another homegrown influence on the "less is more" trend. Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing. In his Case Study House, Ralph Rapson may have mispredicted just how the mechanical revolution would impact everyday life — few American families acquired helicopters, though most eventually got clothes dryers — but his belief that self-sufficiency was both desirable and inevitable was widely shared.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
Will the European Union make it? The question would have sounded strange not long ago. Now even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a "Bermuda triangle" of debt, population decline and lower growth.

As well as those chronic problems, the EU faces an acute crisis in its economic core, the 16 countries that use the single currency. Markets have lost faith that the euro zone's economies, weaker or stronger, will one day converge thanks to the discipline of sharing a single currency, which denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation.

Yet the debate about how to save Europe's single currency from disintegration is stuck. It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise.

Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey. These might include threats to freeze EU funds for poorer regions and EU mega-projects, and even the suspension of a country's voting rights in EU ministerial councils. It insists that economic co-ordination should involve all 27 members of the EU club, among whom there is a small majority for free-market liberalism and economic rigour; in the inner core alone, Germany fears, a small majority favour French interference.

A "southern" camp headed by France wants something different: "European economic government" within an inner core of euro-zone members. Translated, that means politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers. Finally, figures close to the French government have murmured, euro-zone members should agree to some fiscal and social harmonisation: e.g., curbing competition in corporate-tax rates or labour costs.

It is too soon to write off the EU. It remains the world's largest trading block. At its best, the European project is remarkably liberal: built around a single market of 27 rich and poor countries, its internal borders are far more open to goods, capital and labour than any comparable trading area. It is an ambitious attempt to blunt the sharpest edges of globalisation, and make capitalism benign.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Leading doctors today weigh in on the debate over the government's role in promoting public health by demanding that ministers impose "fat taxes" on unhealthy food and introduce cigarette-style warnings to children about the dangers of a poor diet.

The demands follow comments made last week by the health secretary, Andrew Lansley, who insisted the government could not force people to make healthy choices and promised to free businesses from public health regulations.

But senior medical figures want to stop fast-food outlets opening near schools, restrict advertising of products high in fat, salt or sugar, and limit sponsorship of sports events by fast-food producers such as McDonald's.

They argue that government action is necessary to curb Britain's addiction to unhealthy food and help halt spiraling rates of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. Professor Terence Stephenson, president of the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, said that the consumption of unhealthy food should be seen to be just as damaging as smoking or excessive drinking.

"Thirty years ago, it would have been inconceivable to have imagined a ban on smoking in the workplace or in pubs, and yet that is what we have now. Are we willing to be just as courageous in respect of obesity? I would suggest that we should be," said the leader of the UK's children's doctors.

Lansley has alarmed health campaigners by suggesting he wants industry rather than government to take the lead. He said that manufacturers of crisps and candies could play a central role in the Change4Life campaign, the centrepiece of government efforts to boost healthy eating and fitness. He has also criticised the celebrity chef Jamie Oliver's high-profile attempt to improve school lunches in England as an example of how "lecturing" people was not the best way to change their behaviour.

Stephenson suggested potential restrictions could include banning TV advertisements for foods high in fat, salt or sugar before 9 pm and limiting them on billboards or in cinemas. "If we were really bold, we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes — by setting strict limits on advertising, product placement and sponsorship of sports events," he said.

Such a move could affect firms such as McDonald's, which sponsors the youth coaching scheme run by the Football Association. Fast-food chains should also stop offering "inducements" such as toys, cute animals and mobile phone credit to lure young customers, Stephenson said.

Professor Dinesh Bhugra, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, said: "If children are taught about the impact that food has on their growth, and that some things can harm, at least information is available up front."

He also urged councils to impose "fast-food-free zones" around schools and hospitals — areas within which takeaways cannot open.

A Department of Health spokesperson said: "We need to create a new vision for public health where all of society works together to get healthy and live longer. This includes creating a new 'responsibility deal' with business, built on social responsibility, not state regulation. Later this year, we will publish a white paper setting out exactly how we will achieve this."

The food industry will be alarmed that such senior doctors back such radical moves, especially the call to use some of the tough tactics that have been deployed against smoking over the last decade.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义 + 常识 + 固定搭配。
［解题思路］首段先指出互联网匿名制有利于保护隐私和言论自由，第二句转折指出“但恰恰是这种匿名制导致了席卷互联网的网络犯罪激增”。sweep across 意为“席卷，横扫”，“has swept across the Web”既与前文 explosion（激增）相呼应，又凸显网络犯罪传播之广、影响之大，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］skipped（蹦跳着穿过）；［C］walked（步行穿过）；［D］ridden（乘车或骑马穿过）。三者虽可与表示实体的网（如蜘蛛网）搭配，但无法与虚拟的互联网（the Web）及抽象主语 cyber-crime 构成“主体—动作”逻辑，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内逻辑关系 + 过渡段承上启下功能。
［解题思路］第二段（独句过渡段）提出疑问：能否在保护隐私的同时，给似乎越来越不受法律约束的互联网世界带来安全感？此处“privacy be preserved”与“bringing safety and security to a world”分别对应首段匿名制的两面，需要表示“同时，兼顾”的连词衔接。while 可引导时间/对比状语从句（从句主语与主句一致时可省略主语与 be 动词），体现“保护隐私与保障安全并存”，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］for 表目的或原因，但隐私与安全属于并存诉求，并非“方法—目的”或“果—因”关系；［B］within 后应接名词，不能直接衔接分词短语 bringing；［D］though 表让步，“尽管带来安全感，隐私能否被保护”逻辑不通。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 上下文呼应。
［解题思路］空格位于定语从句“that seems increasingly [3]”中修饰 a world（指互联网世界）。结合句中“带来安全感（bringing safety and security）”及首段“网络犯罪激增、席卷互联网”，可知目前的互联网世界缺乏法制与安全保障。lawless 意为“无法无天的，不受法律约束的”，精准概括当前网络世界的混乱与危险，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］careless（粗心的，疏忽的），不能用于修饰“网络世界”本身；［C］pointless（无意义的，无目标的）与［D］helpless（无助的，无望的）均与后文积极寻求安全解决方案的基调不符，且偏离“缺乏法律与安全秩序”的语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 上下文逻辑。
［解题思路］空格句指出，上月美国国家网络安全顾问霍华德·施密特向联邦政府提交了一项旨在让网络更安全的[4]——即建立“自愿的可信身份”系统。由 offer sb. sth. 结构及破折号后的同位语内容可知，这是针对网络安全的正式“提议，提案”（proposal），故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］reason（理由，原因），不能以具体系统方案作同位语；［B］reminder（提醒物），不符合向政府提交具体制度方案的语境；［C］compromise（妥协，折中方案），文中并未提及这是多方退让后的折中产物，下文完全围绕该方案的功能与价值展开。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 比喻对应。
［解题思路］定语从句指出，“自愿的可信身份”系统将是实物钥匙、指纹和带照片身份证的高科技[5]。“实物钥匙、指纹、身份证”均是线下验证身份的工具，因此线上虚拟的身份系统与它们在功能上属于“等同物，等效替代品”（equivalent），故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］information（信息）与［C］entertainment（娱乐）均无法概括“钥匙、指纹、身份证”的身份认证功能；［B］interference（干涉，干扰）带有消极阻碍含义，与“提升网络安全”相悖。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 固定搭配。
［解题思路］逗号后的分词短语“all rolled [6] one”补充说明前文的“实物钥匙、指纹和带照片身份证”与该系统之间的关系。all rolled into one 为固定习语，意为“把多种特性集于一身，融为一体”，强调该高科技系统集多种线下验证功能于一体，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］by 表被动施动者；［C］from 表来源；［D］over 表在……上方或翻越。三者均不能与 rolled...one 构成“融为一体”的惯用表达，代入后逻辑均不通。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 固定搭配。
［解题思路］句子指出该系统可使用智能身份证，或[7]到特定计算机的数字证书，在各类在线服务中验证用户身份。只有当数字证书与特定计算机“连接、绑定”时才能发挥验证作用。linked to 意为“与……相连/关联”，符合技术常识与上下文，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］directed to（指向，对准），无法体现证书与计算机的绑定；［C］chained to 含“被束缚、难以脱身”的消极语义，不符语境；［D］compared to（与……相比），“证书”与“计算机”并非同类可比对象。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义 + 动词辨析。
［解题思路］本句承接上段提交的新提案，进一步阐释该系统的构建理念：其想法是[8]一个私人在线身份系统联盟（a federation of private online identity systems）。由于该系统是针对网络安全问题提出的新方案，应表示“创建，建立”（create），引出下文用户的操作流程，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］dismiss（摒弃，不予考虑）与构想新系统的态度相反；［B］discover（发现已存在之物）与新提案尚待构建的属性不符；［D］improve（改善已有事物）同样不符合首次提出新系统的语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义 + 动作逻辑。
［解题思路］前句说明要创建由多个私人在线身份系统组成的“联盟”，本句接着说明操作流程：用户可以[9]要加入哪一个系统，并且只有身份经过验证的注册用户才能访问这些系统。既然存在多个并行系统，用户自然拥有自主“选择，挑选”（select）的权利，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］recall（回忆，记起），加入新系统并非过去发生的事；［B］suggest（建议），用户是系统使用者，此处决定权在于挑选而非提议；［D］realize（意识到），前文未给出供认知发现的前提信息。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 常识 + 动宾搭配。
［解题思路］本句将该新方案与“需要由政府[10]网络驾照（即网络通行证）”的方案进行对比。在英语中，官方机构正式签发、颁发证件（passports / visas / licenses）的标准动词为 issue，此处过去分词 issued 作后置定语，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］released（发布消息、释放）；［C］distributed（分发物品给大众，如赈灾物资）；［D］delivered（投递信件包裹或发表演讲）。三者均不与 official license 构成“签发证件”的标准搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义 + 固定短语辨析。
［解题思路］句中引号提示的“single sign-on” systems（单点登录系统）是解答关键：谷歌、微软等公司已拥有这类系统，使用户只需[11]一次就能使用多种不同服务。“log in”为计算机专用词组，意为“登录，登入（系统）”，与 single sign-on 形成直接语义复现，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］carry on（继续进行）和［B］linger on（逗留，继续存留）均表示动作持续，与 just once（仅一次）矛盾；［C］set in（坏事开始并持续）无“登录系统”之意。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段间逻辑关系 + 副词短语辨析。
［解题思路］第五段说明系统可“单点登录”，第六段紧接着用比喻揭示其效果：[12]，这种方式将在网络空间中创建一个“围墙花园”，用安全的“街区”和明亮的“路灯”营造安全感。前后段属于对同一方案功能的递进阐释与实质总结，In effect（实际上，事实上）恰能引出其实质作用，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］In vain（徒劳地）含负面色彩，与建立安全环境相悖；［C］In return（作为回报）强调等价交换，两段间不存在交换关系；［D］In contrast（相比之下）表对比，但第六段与第五段谈论的是同一个系统（the approach）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 主旨呼应。
［解题思路］第六段用“围墙花园（walled garden）”“安全街区（safe neighborhoods）”“明亮路灯（bright streetlights）”构建安全可靠的隐喻场景，目的在于营造一种[13]社区感。trusted（可信的，可靠的）不仅契合该隐喻，也与第三段“voluntary trusted identity”形成词汇复现，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］modernized（现代化的）、［C］thriving（繁荣兴旺的）、［D］competing（相互竞争的）虽可修饰 community，但均偏离了全文围绕“网络信任与安全”的核心语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 上下文逻辑。
［解题思路］第七段引述施密特的描述：在这个“自发生态系统”中，个人和组织能够[14]地完成在线交易，彼此信任对方的身份以及交易运行平台的身份。由后文伴随状语“trusting the identities...”可知，这种信任机制让交易双方得以“满怀信任地、放心地”（with confidence）完成交易，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］caution（谨慎小心）意味着对系统安全仍有戒心，与“trusting”矛盾；［B］delight（高兴）偏离“信任与安全”主线；［D］patience（耐心）暗示流程繁琐耗时，文中并无体现。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 介词搭配。
［解题思路］定语从句“[15] which the transaction runs”修饰 the infrastructure（此处指网络基础设施/平台），还原语序为“the transaction runs [15] the infrastructure”。英语中表示交易、程序“在某平台/系统上运行”，固定搭配为 run on，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］run after（追逐）；［C］run beyond（超越，脱离），交易脱离平台无法体现平台安全；［D］run across（偶然遇见，跑过），均不符合“交易在基础设施上运行”的语义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义 + 动词辨析。
［解题思路］第八段开头 Still（尽管如此）笔锋一转，由前文介绍系统优势转向引发的争议。紧接着下句指出“Some applaud the approach; others are concerned”（有人赞同，有人担忧）。可见该计划在隐私权活跃分子中“造成了意见分歧”，divided（使产生分歧）恰能概括后句两极反应，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］disappointed（使失望）仅能覆盖担忧者，无法涵盖赞同者（applaud）；［C］protected（保护）脱离讨论主题；［D］united（使团结）与“有人赞同、有人担忧”的分歧现状完全相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 逻辑呼应。
［解题思路］句中“an initiative push（最初的推动）”与后文“a compulsory Internet 'driver's license' mentality（强制性的网络通行证模式）”构成“起点—终点”的演变链条，说明隐私权活跃分子担忧该计划“最终、归根结底”（eventually）会滑向强制性网络驾照制度，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］frequently（频繁地）、［B］incidentally（偶然地，附带地）、［C］occasionally（偶尔地）均描述动作频率或偶发性，既无法与 initiative 构成演进呼应，也不符合对尚未全面推行的政府计划的趋势预测。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段间并列关系 + 句内语义。
［解题思路］第九段开头 also 提示与第八段形成并列，继续阐述另一群体对政府计划的负面反应：该计划也受到一些计算机安全专家的[18]，他们担心（worry）该系统仍会使互联网大部分区域处于危险之中。由 worry 可知专家们持“怀疑、质疑”（skepticism）态度，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］tolerance（容忍，虽有不满但仍接受）；［C］indifference（漠不关心）与 worry 所体现的关切相悖；［D］enthusiasm（热情支持）属于积极态度，与专家们的担忧正相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 情感色彩一致。
［解题思路］安全专家担心（worry）施密特设想的“自发生态系统”仍然（still）会使大部分互联网处于[19]的状态。“still”呼应首段网络犯罪猖獗的现状，因此此处应填入消极词，表示“易受攻击的，脆弱的”（vulnerable），故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］manageable（可管理的）与［B］defendable（可防御的）均为正面评价，与安全专家的担忧态度冲突；［D］invisible（无形的）虽符合互联网物理属性，但并非专家担心的安全隐患。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义 + 类比推理。
［解题思路］末句通过“in the same way that drivers must be licensed...”进行类比：既然司机“必须（must）”考取驾照才能上路，那么这些持质疑态度的安全专家就主张所有互联网用户都应该被[20]注册并验证身份。forced（被强制，被迫）与 must 语义一致，体现强制性监管，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］invited（被邀请）与［C］allowed（被允许）均不具备强制力；［B］appointed（被委任，指派担任职务），对象通常是特定人员而非全体网民。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Ms. Simmons was criticized for

options.text: leaving the board in tough times
options.content: leaving the board in tough times

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1、Ms. Simmons 及 criticized 定位至第一段第三句。
［命题解密］该句先以“was under fire for having sat on Goldman's compensation committee”点明西蒙斯在高盛薪酬委员会任职期间遭受猛烈抨击，随后分号后的反问句“how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked?”点破批评实质：她本应监督高管薪酬，却放任巨额奖金支出毫无察觉地通过，即“未能履行自身职责（failing to fulfill her duty）”，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“gaining excessive profits”将“放任高盛发放巨额奖金”偷换为“她自己获取超额收益”；［C］“refusing to make compromises”是对“let...pass unremarked”的望文生义；［D］“leaving the board in tough times”因果倒置，离开董事会是遭受抨击后的结果而非受批评的原因。

questions.stem: We learn from Paragraph 2 that outside directors are supposed to be
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 2 及 outside directors are supposed to be 定位至第二段第一、二句。
［命题解密］第二段首句直接指出“Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm's board”（外部董事应当在公司董事会中担任有益且较少偏见的顾问），第二句补充说明他们拥有足够独立性（enough independence）去质疑首席执行官的提案。综合可见，外部董事应是“独立的顾问（independent advisers）”，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“generous investors”曲解了第二句中“made their wealth...elsewhere”（在别处已积累财富）的含义；［B］“unbiased executives”将“advisers（顾问）”偷换为“executives（高管）”；［C］“share price forecasters”属于无中生有，第三句仅指“股价下跌时提供建议”，而非“预测股价”。

questions.stem: According to the researchers from Ohio University, after an outside director's surprise departure, the firm is likely to

options.text: do less well in the stock market
options.content: do less well in the stock market

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 researchers from Ohio University 及 surprise departure 定位至第三段第四、五句。
［命题解密］这两句明确列举了外部董事突然离职后的三项后果：公司不得不重申盈利的概率上升近 20%、被列入联邦集体诉讼的可能性增加，以及公司股票表现可能更差（the stock is likely to perform worse）。［C］“do less well in the stock market”是对“the stock is likely to perform worse”的精准同义改写，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“become more stable”张冠李戴，原文末句指外部董事往往跳槽前往更稳定的大公司（more stable firms），而非原公司变稳定；［B］“report increased earnings”将“restate earnings（被迫重申盈利）”曲解为“报告盈利增长”；［D］“perform worse in lawsuits”偷换主语且过度推理，原文仅说被卷入集体诉讼的可能性增加，且“perform worse”针对的是公司股票而非诉讼表现。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that outside directors

options.text: may stay for the attractive offers from the firm
options.content: may stay for the attractive offers from the firm

options.text: have often had records of wrongdoings in the firm
options.content: have often had records of wrongdoings in the firm

options.text: are accustomed to stress-free work in the firm
options.content: are accustomed to stress-free work in the firm

options.text: will decline incentives from the firm
options.content: will decline incentives from the firm

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 the last paragraph 定位至第四段第二、三句。
［命题解密］末段指出，由于外部董事在坏消息曝光前离职更容易保住声誉，因此“Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives”（想要在艰难时期留住外部董事的公司或许必须制定激励措施），否则他们就会像西蒙斯一样离开。由此合理推知，若公司提供有吸引力的条件（attractive offers 对应 incentives），外部董事可能会选择留下，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］“have often had records of wrongdoings”偷换主语，原文“any wrongdoing occurred”指公司发生不当行为时董事刚好在职，并非董事自身有劣迹；［C］“stress-free work”曲解了“have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations”（更容易避免声誉受损）；［D］“will decline incentives”与末两句“靠激励留人，否则就走（Otherwise...）”的逻辑正好相反。

questions.stem: The author's attitude toward the role of outside directors is
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］本题考察作者对全文核心对象 outside directors 的态度，综合定位第二至四段。
［命题解密］第二段肯定外部董事能作为有益、少偏见、独立的顾问在危机中建言献策；第三段虽指出其突然离职会给公司带来负面冲击，但也特意澄清这并不意味着他们都在“跳离沉船”，而是常常正常“另谋高就”；第四段更是建议公司在艰难时期创设激励机制留住外部董事。可见作者充分肯定其价值与正面作用，持肯定态度（positive），故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“permissive（放任纵容的）”属于无中生有，作者主张用激励制度留住外部董事，并非纵容不负责任；［C］“scornful（蔑视的）”与［D］“critical（批评的）”均以偏概全，仅着眼于外部董事为避嫌而离职的现象，忽视了作者在第二、四段对其作用的正面肯定。

questions.stem: By saying "Newspapers like... their own doom" (Lines 3-4, Para. 1), the author indicates that newspapers
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干定位至第一段第四句“Newspapers like the San Francisco Chronicle were chronicling their own doom”。
［命题解密］首段开篇先点明一年前（A year ago）报业末日似乎近在咫尺（the end seemed near），经济衰退差点夺走仅存的广告与读者，随后以《旧金山纪事报》“都在记录着自己的末日/劫数”为例，形象说明一年前报业曾深陷绝境（in a desperate situation），以此反衬如今形势的逆转，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“neglected the sign of crisis”将第二段首句“现在几乎看不到危机的迹象（little sign of crisis）”篡改为“报业忽视危机迹象”；［B］“failed to get state subsidies”与［C］“were not charitable corporations”均曲解了后文联邦贸易委员会的设问“Should they become charitable corporations? Should the state subsidize them?”，把讨论中的拯救方案误作既定否定事实。

questions.stem: Some newspapers refused delivery to distant suburbs probably because

options.text: journalists reported little about these areas
options.content: journalists reported little about these areas

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 refused delivery to distant suburbs 定位至第三段第四句，并结合上下句语境分析。
［命题解密］第三段指出，多家报纸为了维持运营（stayed afloat）不惜大幅裁员、涨价瘦身，甚至“胆敢拒绝向偏远郊区投递报纸”，紧接着第五句将这些举措称为“不得已的求生举措（desperate measures）”，且证明行之有效。由于偏远郊区投递成本高、利润低，报社拒绝配送显然是为了“削减成本（reduce costs）”以求生存，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“readers threatened to pay less”与前句“Readers are paying more”（读者付出更多）正相反；［C］“journalists reported little about these areas”无中生有，文中未提及郊区新闻报道量少；［D］“subscribers complained about slimmer products”将“瘦身”和“拒送郊区”两项并列自救措施强行拼接为因果关系，且文中并未提及订户抱怨。

questions.stem: Compared with their American counterparts, Japanese newspapers are much more stable because they
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Japanese newspapers are much more stable 定位至第四段第二至五句。
［命题解密］第四段首先点出报纸正变得更加平衡，接着指出美国报纸长期以来极度依赖广告（reliance on ads），2008 年高达 87% 的收入来自广告；而在日本这一比例仅为 35%，因此毫不意外日本报纸要稳定得多。可见日本报业更稳定的核心原因在于“对广告的依赖更少（less dependent on advertising）”，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“have more sources of revenue”错误，首句明言报纸收入均来自“readers and advertisers”两大渠道，美日并无渠道数量差异；［B］“have more balanced newsrooms”将“more balanced businesses（商业模式更均衡）”偷换为“新闻编辑室”；［D］“are less affected by readership”与数据相反，日本广告占比仅 35%，说明来自读者的发行收入占比更高（65%），受读者群影响反而更大。

questions.stem: What can be inferred from the last paragraph about the current newspaper business?

options.text: Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.
options.content: Distinctiveness is an essential feature of newspapers.

options.text: Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspapers.
options.content: Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspapers.

options.text: Foreign bureaus play a crucial role in the newspaper business.
options.content: Foreign bureaus play a crucial role in the newspaper business.

options.text: Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews.
options.content: Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews.

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 the last paragraph 定位至第五段。
［命题解密］末段指出，横扫编辑室的裁员潮虽波及所有人，但大部分裁撤集中在“报纸最缺乏特色的领域（where newspapers are least distinctive）”，如汽车和电影评论、大众商业及驻外机构，结果报纸不再求全，因为“完整性在报业已不再是美德（completeness is no longer a virtue）”。反向推知，当今报业生存的关键在于“独特性是不可或缺的特征（Distinctiveness is an essential feature）”，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］“Completeness is to blame for the failure of newspapers”强加因果，原文仅说求全不再是优势，未将其归咎为破产元凶；［C］“Foreign bureaus play a crucial role”与原文“驻外办事处遭到无情裁撤”相反；［D］“Readers have lost their interest in car and film reviews”无中生有，这些版块被裁是因为缺乏独特性而非读者失去兴趣。

questions.stem: The most appropriate title for this text would be

options.text: American Newspapers: Gone with the Wind
options.content: American Newspapers: Gone with the Wind

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］本题为主旨标题题，统筹定位全文各段主旨。
［命题解密］第一、二段指出曾被预言濒死的美国报业通过自救重获盈利；第三段详述裁员、涨价、停送偏远郊区等艰难求生手段；第四段说明收入结构日趋健康；末段点出舍弃求全、立足特色的生存之道。全篇紧扣美国报业在危机中“挣扎求生（Struggling for Survival）”的历程，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］“Gone with the Wind（随风而逝）”和［D］“A Hopeless Story（毫无希望的故事）”均停留在一年前悲观预言的基调上，与全文“死里逃生、重现盈利”的主基调矛盾；［C］“A Thriving Business（蓬勃兴旺的行业）”则过度拔高，原文第二、三段明确指出利润率远不如前且过程艰难（Not the 20% profit margins... It has not been much fun）。

questions.stem: The postwar American housing style largely reflected the Americans'
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 postwar American housing style 定位至第二段。
［命题解密］第二段明确指出，在住宅建筑上战后是一个崇尚“少即是多（less could truly be more）”的时期；在大萧条与战争期间，美国人学会了节俭生活，“而正是这种克制（restraint），加之战后对未来的信心（postwar confidence），使得小巧高效的住宅成为流行风尚”。由此直接对应［C］“restraint and confidence”，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“prosperity and growth”是第一段对二战后总体社会背景的惯常印象，作者在第二段用 But 转折引出住宅风格的节俭取向；［B］“efficiency and practicality”中的高效是住宅本身的物理特点，而非美国人的精神心态；［D］“pride and faithfulness”将“confidence”过度曲解为对国家的自豪与忠诚，于文无据。

questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from Paragraph 3 about the Bauhaus?

options.text: It was founded by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.
options.content: It was founded by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

options.text: Its designing concept was affected by World War II.
options.content: Its designing concept was affected by World War II.

options.text: Most American architects used to be associated with it.
options.content: Most American architects used to be associated with it.

options.text: It had a great influence upon American architecture.
options.content: It had a great influence upon American architecture.

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 3 及 the Bauhaus 定位至第三段第二、三句。
［命题解密］第三段指出，“少即是多”由德国建筑师密斯推广，他和其他与包豪斯设计学院（the Bauhaus）有关的设计师在二战前移民美国并在美国建筑院校任教；紧接着第三句总结：“These designers came to exert enormous influence on the course of American architecture”（这些设计师对美国建筑业的发展进程产生了巨大影响）。由此可推知，包豪斯学院对美国建筑影响深远，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“founded by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe”无中生有，原文仅说密斯“associated with the Bauhaus（与包豪斯有关）”，未提由他创立；［B］“designing concept was affected by World War II”偷换概念，二战只是这批设计师移民美国的时间节点；［C］“Most American architects used to be associated with it”张冠李戴，与包豪斯有关的是移民美国的德国设计师，而非多数美国建筑师。

questions.stem: Mies held that elegance of architectural design

options.text: was not reliant on abundant decoration
options.content: was not reliant on abundant decoration

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Mies 及 elegance of architectural design 定位至第四段第一、二句。
［命题解密］第四段首句说明密斯的标志性名言意为“布局得当的精简装饰比繁复堆砌更具震撼力”，第二句紧接着点明其理念核心：“Elegance, he believed, did not derive from abundance”（他认为优雅并非来源于繁复冗余）。［C］“was not reliant on abundant decoration”是对“did not derive from abundance”的精准同义替换，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“related to large space”与［B］“identified with emptiness”均误解了末句的“masked the fact that the spaces he designed were small and efficient, rather than big and often empty”，原文意为密斯的设计实为“小而精”而非“大而空”；［D］“not associated with efficiency”与文中强调的“small and efficient”正好相反。

questions.stem: What is true about the apartments Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive?

options.text: They were built with materials popular at that time.
options.content: They were built with materials popular at that time.

options.text: They were more spacious than neighboring buildings.
options.content: They were more spacious than neighboring buildings.

options.text: They shared some characteristics of abstract art.
options.content: They shared some characteristics of abstract art.

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 apartments Mies built on Chicago's Lake Shore Drive 定位至第五段。
［命题解密］第五段首句将湖滨大道公寓与邻近老旧建筑对比，指出其面积更小；第二句解释其大受欢迎的原因，末尾将其建筑细节与比例的优雅直接称为“the architectural equivalent of the abstract art so popular at the time”（当时盛行的抽象艺术在建筑上的体现）。因此这些公寓具备抽象艺术的某些特征，故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“ignored details and proportions”与原文因“elegance of the buildings' details and proportions”而受欢迎正相反；［B］“materials popular at that time”与第四段“materials...that in the 1940s symbolized the future（在当时尚属于超前象征而非流行普及）”相悖；［C］“more spacious than neighboring buildings”与第五段首句“smaller...than those in their older neighbors”直接冲突。

questions.stem: What can we learn about the design of the "Case Study Houses"?

options.text: Natural scenes were taken into consideration.
options.content: Natural scenes were taken into consideration.

options.text: Details were sacrificed for the overall effect.
options.content: Details were sacrificed for the overall effect.

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 design of the "Case Study Houses" 定位至第七段第一、二句。
［命题解密］末段在介绍“案例研究住宅”时，第二句明确阐述其设计美学来源：“Aesthetic effect came from the landscape, new materials and forthright detailing”（审美效果源自自然景观、新材料和直观明了的细节处理）。［B］“Natural scenes were taken into consideration”中的 Natural scenes 恰是原文 landscape 的同义替换，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“Mechanical devices were widely used”曲解了末句，拉尔夫·雷普森只是预言机械革命，但“很少有家庭购买直升机”；［C］“Details were sacrificed”与原文“forthright detailing（注重简洁明了的细节）”相反；［D］“Eco-friendly materials”将“landscape”和“new materials”强行嫁接，原文并未提及材料是否“环保”。

questions.stem: The EU is faced with so many problems that

options.text: it has more or less lost faith in markets
options.content: it has more or less lost faith in markets

options.text: even its supporters begin to feel concerned
options.content: even its supporters begin to feel concerned

options.text: some of its member countries plan to abandon euro
options.content: some of its member countries plan to abandon euro

options.text: it intends to deny the possibility of devaluation
options.content: it intends to deny the possibility of devaluation

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 The EU is faced with so many problems 定位至第一段第三句。
［命题解密］首段开篇先发问“欧盟还能挺过去吗？”，随后第三句用 Now 引出严峻现实：“even the project's greatest cheerleaders talk of a continent facing a 'Bermuda triangle' of debt, population decline and lower growth”（就连欧盟项目最狂热的支持者也在谈论欧洲大陆正面临债务、人口下降和增长放缓的“百慕大三角”）。cheerleaders 对应选项中的 supporters，说明连支持者也开始感到担忧，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“lost faith in markets”偷换主语，第二段第二句是“Markets have lost faith（市场失去信心）”，而非欧盟对市场失去信心；［C］“plan to abandon euro”无中生有，第二、三段讨论的是如何挽救单一货币而非计划放弃；［D］“intends to deny the possibility of devaluation”曲解了“denies uncompetitive members the quick fix of devaluation”，意为使用单一货币客观上使成员国无法靠本币贬值救急，并非欧盟有意“否定贬值可能性”。

questions.stem: The debate over the EU's single currency is stuck because the dominant powers

options.text: are competing for the leading position
options.content: are competing for the leading position

options.text: are busy handling their own crises
options.content: are busy handling their own crises

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 debate over the EU's single currency is stuck 定位至第三段第二句。
［命题解密］第三段明确解释了僵局的原因：“It is stuck because the euro zone's dominant powers, France and Germany, agree on the need for greater harmonisation within the euro zone, but disagree about what to harmonise”（之所以陷入僵局，是因为欧元区两大主导国法国和德国虽然都同意需要加强协调统一，但在具体协调什么的问题上意见分歧）。［C］“fail to reach an agreement on harmonisation”精准概括此意，故［C］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“competing for the leading position”无中生有，文中仅客观称法德为 dominant powers，未提争夺领导权；［B］“busy handling their own crises”未在文中提及；［D］“disagree on the steps towards disintegration”曲解文意，法德争论的是如何挽救单一货币免于解体（save...from disintegration），而非解体的步骤。

questions.stem: To solve the euro problem, Germany proposed that

options.text: EU funds for poor regions be increased
options.content: EU funds for poor regions be increased

options.text: only core members be involved in economic co-ordination
options.content: only core members be involved in economic co-ordination

options.text: voting rights of the EU members be guaranteed
options.content: voting rights of the EU members be guaranteed

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 solve the euro problem、Germany proposed 定位至第四段第一句。
［命题解密］第四段首句清晰阐明德国的主张：“Germany thinks the euro must be saved by stricter rules on borrowing, spending and competitiveness, backed by quasi-automatic sanctions for governments that do not obey”（德国认为必须通过对借贷、支出和竞争力制定更严格的规则来拯救欧元，并辅以对违规政府的准自动制裁）。［B］“stricter regulations be imposed”与 stricter rules 完全对应，故［B］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“EU funds for poor regions be increased”与原文“freeze EU funds for poorer regions（威胁冻结贫困地区资金）”正相反；［C］“only core members be involved”张冠李戴，德国坚持所有 27 个成员国都应参与经济协调，仅限核心国是法国的主张；［D］“voting rights...be guaranteed”与原文“suspension of a country's voting rights（暂停投票权）”完全相悖。

questions.stem: The French proposal of handling the crisis implies that

options.text: poor countries are more likely to get funds
options.content: poor countries are more likely to get funds

options.text: strict monetary policy will be applied to poor countries
options.content: strict monetary policy will be applied to poor countries

options.text: loans will be readily available to rich countries
options.content: loans will be readily available to rich countries

options.text: rich countries will basically control Eurobonds
options.content: rich countries will basically control Eurobonds

questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 French proposal 定位至第五段第一、二句。
［命题解密］第五段指出，以法国为首的“南部阵营”主张在欧元区核心国建立“欧洲经济政府”，第二句解释其含义：“politicians intervening in monetary policy and a system of redistribution from richer to poorer members, via cheaper borrowing for governments through common Eurobonds or complete fiscal transfers”（由政客干预货币政策，并通过共同欧元债券提供的低息贷款或全面财政转移支付，建立从富裕成员国向较贫困成员国的收入再分配体制）。由此推知，较贫困国家更有可能获得资金支持，故［A］正确。
［错项排除］［B］“strict monetary policy”与第五段法国主张政客干预货币政策及德国第四段追求的“经济严纪”相悖；［C］“loans will be readily available to rich countries”与“from richer to poorer members”方向颠倒；［D］“rich countries will basically control Eurobonds”属于偷换概念，共同欧元债券是用来资助困难成员国低息借款的工具，文中并未提及由富国控制。

questions.stem: Regarding the future of the EU, the author seems to feel
questions.explanation:
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 future of the EU 及 author seems to feel 定位至第六段（末段）。
［命题解密］末段首句明确表态：“It is too soon to write off the EU”（现在断言欧盟彻底失败还为时过早），随后列举欧盟仍是世界最大贸易集团、内部市场高度自由开放、致力于缓和全球化冲击并使资本主义向善等重大优势。由此可见作者对欧盟的未来抱有信心，持乐观充满希望的态度（hopeful），故［D］正确。
［错项排除］［A］“pessimistic（悲观的）”与［B］“desperate（绝望的）”均与末段“为时过早”及高度肯定欧盟前景的基调完全相反；［C］“conceited（自负的，骄傲自满的）”将作者客观肯定欧盟制度优势曲解为盲目自负，不符合行文态度。

［命题解密］第六段第一、二句指出，卫生大臣兰斯利主张让食品行业而非政府发挥主导作用，并明确表示“manufacturers of crisps and candies could play a central role in the Change4Life campaign”（薯片和糖果生产商可以在“为健康而改变”运动中发挥核心作用）。［E］“the producers of crisps and candies could contribute significantly to the Change4Life campaign”精准同义转述原文，故［E］正确。

［命题解密］第四段末句指出斯蒂芬森认为食用不健康食品应被视作与吸烟同样有害；第七段第二句更直接引述其原话：“we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes — by setting strict limits on...”（我们甚至应当像对待香烟一样对待高热量快餐）。综合第一段医生群体要求向儿童引入香烟式警示语（introduce cigarette-style warnings to children about the dangers of a poor diet）的呼吁，［D］项完整概括了斯蒂芬森的立场，故［D］正确。
